chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (the first Imam), peace be upon him, about a man who prays behind an Imam whom he follows in a prayer where the recitation is recited aloud, but he does not hear the recitation. He said, 'There is no harm whether he remains silent or recites.'
And that which clarifies what we mentioned, that if he hears a voice it suffices for him even if the recitation is not distinct to him, added to what we have presented, is what he narrated:

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.يَقْتَدِي بِهِ: Follows him (referring to following the Imam in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if they cannot hear the Imam's recitation during a loud prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the flexibility in the role of the follower during *Jahri* (audible) prayers, ruling that the prayer is valid whether the follower remains silent or recites Surah Al-Fatihah independently. This supports the Shia view that the follower's recitation is not strictly nullified by the Imam's audible recitation, provided the follower is capable of hearing or performing the act. It highlights the practical leniency granted to worshippers in congregational settings where auditory conditions may vary.
